================================================================================
SQL Server blocks: a procedure with BEGIN ... END after AS
================================================================================

CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.p @a INT, @b NVARCHAR(10) = N'x;' AS
BEGIN
  SET NOCOUNT ON;
  IF @a > 0
  BEGIN
    SELECT @a AS [end];
  END
  ELSE
    SELECT "begin";
END;
EXEC dbo.p 1;

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

(source_file
  (statement
    (string)
    (quoted_identifier)
    (quoted_identifier))
  (statement))

================================================================================
SQL Server blocks: TRY, CATCH and a transaction
================================================================================

CREATE OR ALTER PROC dbo.q AS
BEGIN
  BEGIN TRY
    BEGIN TRANSACTION;
    UPDATE t SET v = CASE WHEN v IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE v END;
    COMMIT TRANSACTION;
  END TRY
  BEGIN CATCH
    ROLLBACK TRAN;
    THROW;
  END CATCH
END;
SELECT 1;

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

(source_file
  (statement)
  (statement))

================================================================================
SQL Server blocks: a trigger and a function
================================================================================

CREATE TRIGGER tr ON t AFTER INSERT AS
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO log SELECT * FROM inserted;
END;
CREATE FUNCTION dbo.f (@x INT) RETURNS INT AS
BEGIN
  RETURN @x + 1;
END;

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

(source_file
  (statement)
  (statement))

================================================================================
SQL Server blocks: a body with no BEGIN ends at its semicolon
================================================================================

CREATE PROCEDURE r AS SELECT 1;
CREATE FUNCTION g () RETURNS TABLE AS RETURN (SELECT 1 AS a);
CREATE PROCEDURE s WITH EXECUTE AS OWNER AS SET NOCOUNT ON;
SELECT 2;

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

(source_file
  (statement)
  (statement)
  (statement)
  (statement))

================================================================================
SQL Server blocks: a variable right after BEGIN and in a nested block
================================================================================

CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.p AS
BEGIN
  :'stmt';
  IF @a > 0
  BEGIN
    :"body";
  END
  SET @a = :{?name};
END;
EXEC dbo.p;

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

(source_file
  (statement
    (variable
      (variable_name))
    (variable
      (variable_name))
    (variable
      (variable_name)))
  (statement))

================================================================================
SQL Server blocks: a character that is not in a word right after BEGIN
================================================================================

CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.p AS BEGIN (SELECT 1); END;
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.q AS BEGIN [t].a = 1; END;
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.r AS BEGIN #t.a = 1; END;
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.s AS BEGIN @a = 1; END;
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.u AS BEGIN 'x'; BEGIN (SELECT 2); END; END;
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.v AS BEGIN TRAN; COMMIT;
EXEC dbo.p;

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

(source_file
  (statement)
  (statement
    (quoted_identifier))
  (statement)
  (statement)
  (statement
    (string))
  (statement)
  (statement)
  (statement))

================================================================================
SQL Server blocks: a name in brackets in a body
================================================================================

CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.p AS BEGIN SELECT 1 AS [a;END;b'c]; END;
select 2;
